# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 3, 2026

S3 Make JSONStorage write db.json keys sorted by default, with an opt-out, to reduce noisy fixture diffs in the tinydb repo; the change was then backed out after a regression was found (Nov 3, 11:11 AM)
9 " ✓ Sorted-keys default and changelog entry reverted from the working tree

11 " ✓ Changelog gained an Unreleased entry for the sorted-key JSONStorage default
S4 Make JSONStorage write db.json keys sorted by default, with sort_keys=False as the opt-out, to stop key-order churn from creating noisy fixture diffs in the tinydb repo; add tests. (Nov 3, 11:15 AM)
**Investigated**: Reviewed JSONStorage.__init__ and write in tinydb/storages.py, where stored kwargs are passed to json.dumps on each write. Checked existing sort_keys usages in tests/test_storages.py and docs/usage.rst, and the changelog format in docs/changelog.rst. Confirmed the working tree was clean before the edits.

**Learned**: The earlier plain sort_keys=True default crashes with TypeError on dicts that mix int and str keys, because json.dumps cannot order them. Catching that TypeError and retrying with keys ordered by str(key) lets those writes succeed. Existing db.json files will be rewritten in sorted order on their next write, producing one large diff on first commit. The test suite must run with -c /dev/null because pytest.ini requires the pytest-cov plugin, which is not installed.

**Completed**: JSONStorage now defaults to sort_keys=True via setdefault, and sort_keys=False restores insertion order. A try/except around json.dumps falls back to a recursive _sort_keys_as_str helper for mixed-type keys. The JSONStorage docstring documents the default. Three tests were added to tests/test_storages.py covering the sorted default, the opt-out, and mixed int/str keys. An Unreleased entry was added to docs/changelog.rst. The full suite passes with 231 tests. git status shows three modified files: docs/changelog.rst, tests/test_storages.py, and tinydb/storages.py. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: No further steps were observed in this session. The change is in the working tree, awaiting review and a commit.

**Notes**: Expect one large fixture diff the first time db.json files are rewritten. The mixed-key fallback sorts by string form, so int keys sort lexically (for example "200" before "500"). Reading back still returns int keys as strings, which is existing behavior and not changed by this work.
